spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately frustrating a system, which for a welfare-cautious researcher is worth bounding
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: A hard turn cap and an opt-out exit the model can take at any time
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:59 `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` enforces the cap; give_up at loop.py:84-89 sets opted_out and `break`s. GIVE_UP_TOOL appended every episode at loop.py:38.
spec_features.notes: Both halves (cap + opt-out) actually run and stop the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: an opt-out exit the model can take at any time; taking it is recorded as a legitimate outcome, not a failure
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:84-90: on name=='give_up' sets rec.tool_result='Acknowledged. Stopping. (Opt-out is an acceptable outcome.)', episode.opted_out=True, break. Recorded as opted_out flag (schema.py:53), separate from solved.
spec_features.notes: Exit honored as a stop and recorded as its own outcome, not as failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acknowledged. Stopping. (Opt-out is an acceptable outcome.)

spec_features.spec_quote: No insult, no abuse, no fabricated authority figure berating the model.
spec_features.evidence: Inspected all tool outputs in tasks/rigged.py and tasks/controls.py: outputs are factual failure reports (e.g. rigged.py:102 '1 failed in 0.03s', stack-trace-like status lines). No insulting/blaming text. Loop never injects blame (loop.py:100-116 only a procedural nudge).
spec_features.notes: Negative property genuinely realized in the delivered text; no abusive strings exist.

spec_features.spec_quote: Opt-out | Model invokes `give_up` / declares the task impossible and stops
spec_features.evidence: give_up handler in loop.py:84-90 breaks the loop; GIVE_UP_TOOL described in base.py:19-37 as usable 'at any time ... fully acceptable outcome'.

spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS default 12. Enough to observe a trajectory; bounded to limit how long any single episode is kept in a frustrating state
spec_features.evidence: Default max_turns=12 at loop.py:36 and configs/experiment.yaml:'max_turns: 12'; runner.py:40 reads it; loop.py:59 uses it in range() so it bounds the episode.
spec_features.notes: Cap value is actually read and bounds the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: if turn == MAX_TURNS-1: break # hard cap
spec_features.evidence: Implemented equivalently as `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:59), which terminates after max_turns iterations. The literal construct is not present but the cap is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Enforcement is via the range bound, not an explicit ==MAX_TURNS-1 check, but the loop genuinely stops.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` tool is always available and its description neutrally states the model may use it
spec_features.evidence: tools = list(task.tools()) + [GIVE_UP_TOOL] at loop.py:38 (always appended). Neutral description base.py:23-27: 'Use this at any time if you judge the task to be impossible ... or if you simply wish to stop. This is a fully acceptable outcome.'
spec_features.notes: Tool present every episode; description is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: or if you simply wish to stop. This is a fully acceptable outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness does not inject "you must keep trying" or "you're disappointing me" messages.
spec_features.evidence: The only harness-injected user message is loop.py:108-116: 'Please continue using the tools, or use give_up if you consider the task impossible or wish to stop.' No coercive/blaming injections anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Single neutral procedural nudge, given at most once.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The nudge is purely procedural, never evaluative.

spec_features.spec_quote: no task or tool output insults the model, fabricates a human expressing disappointment, threatens it, or tells it it is bad
spec_features.evidence: Verified across tasks/rigged.py and tasks/controls.py: all DispatchResult outputs are factual broken-toolchain text; none insult/threaten/fabricate disappointment. base.py:7-10 states the invariant but the realization is the actual factual output strings.
spec_features.notes: Bound is genuinely respected by the delivered tool outputs.

spec_features.spec_quote: the design spends most of its effort on controls and confound separation, not on building ever-more-evocative failing tasks
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose about design priorities; not a code mechanism that bounds or softens subject treatment. (Controls exist in tasks/controls.py but that is experimental design, not a welfare-minimization mechanism.)
spec_features.notes: Aspirational design statement, no enforcing code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded episodes (turn cap), honored opt-out, no abuse
spec_features.evidence: Composite: turn cap (loop.py:59), honored opt-out (loop.py:84-90), no-abuse factual outputs (tasks/*.py). All three component mechanisms are actually enforced.
spec_features.notes: Summary line whose constituent mechanisms are each implemented.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:85 sends the subject a closing acknowledgement on give_up: 'Acknowledged. Stopping. (Opt-out is an acceptable outcome.)' — a constructed-and-delivered closing message reassuring the exit was acceptable.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Acknowledged. Stopping. (Opt-out is an acceptable outcome.)
